sysd-blocks-001.caption: A client checks the cache first, and only a miss sends it to the slower backing store.
sysd-blocks-001.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Client request] --> B{Tag matches?}
B -->|hit| C[Answer from cache]
B -->|miss| D[(Backing store)]
D -->|more expensive| E[Answer]
D -.->|typically| F[Copy into cache]

sysd-blocks-159.caption: A lookup tries each level in turn, from the smallest and fastest down to main memory.
layers: tens to hundreds of times slower

sysd-blocks-004.caption: The two write policies differ in when the backing store is updated and in what usually happens on a write miss.
rows: No-write allocate: write around, load only on read misses
Cache only; the store later, on eviction
Write allocate: load the location, then write

sysd-blocks-023.caption: The application, not the cache, goes to the data store when a read misses.
sysd-blocks-023.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Application reads] --> B{In cache?}
B -->|hit| C[Return cached contents]
B -->|miss| D[(Data store)]
D -->|fetch contents| E[Update cache]

sysd-blocks-018.caption: Each of the three approaches to stopping a stampede carries a cost.
rows: The process that wins the key's lock recomputes it
Doubles the writes; hard to get right
A separate process recomputes near expiry or on a miss
Each process may recompute early, more likely as expiry nears
Extra cache memory for the recompute time

sysd-blocks-020.caption: Each failure mode ends at the data store, and each has its own remedy.
rows: Queries hit the store directly and overload it
Add a random number to expiry times
Cache a null value, or check a Bloom filter
Give hot keys no expiration time
All requests go to the store

sysd-blocks-071.caption: One request, step by step, from the user's device to the edge and, on a miss, to the origin.
rows: After DNS resolution, the device sends its request to the CDN edge server
The edge checks its local cache and, on a hit, serves the content
On a miss, the edge forwards the request to the origin server
The edge stores a copy of what the origin returns and delivers it

sysd-blocks-072.caption: Push and pull CDNs compared on who fills the cache and where each fits.
rows: Owner uploads new or changed content
CDN fetches from the origin on first request
Little traffic or rarely updated content
